summary: Arindam Chakrabarti is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his DPhil from the University of Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Delhi, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Stony Brook University.
Arindam Mondal is an Indologist who completed his M.Phil. at Jadavpur University. He has served as an Assistant Professor at Shishuram Das College.

Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies, completing a Research MA at Leiden University, attested in 2018. Jonker studied under Peter C. Bisschop, Daniele Cuneo, and Jonathan A. Silk.
Arion Roşu (1924–2007) studied at the University of Bucharest from circa 1943 to 1947 and at the University of Paris from circa 1965 to 1974, where he was a student of Jean Filliozat.

Aristotle C. Dy works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned PhD degrees from Ateneo de Manila University and SOAS University of London under Antonello Palumbo, later serving as Lecturer at Ateneo and President of Xavier School.
Aritri Dutta is an external PhD student in Tibetology and religious studies at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Henk Blezer, attested in 2026.

Arjo Vanderjagt (born 1948) is a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arjuna S. R. works in computational fields, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at Karnataka Samskrit University and earning a PhD from the University of Hyderabad (2012–2017), he held administrative and research posts at Manipal Academy of Higher Education.

Arlo Griffiths (born 1976) works in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. Educated at Harvard and Leiden University under Henk Bodewitz, he has held posts at Groningen, Leiden, the Kern Institute, and as professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Armand Guérinot (1872–1940) was an Indologist who studied at Bonn and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Lyon under Hermann Jacobi and Paul Regnaud. In 1909, he worked as a typographical proofreader at the Imprimerie Nationale.

Armand Minard (1906–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, EPHE, and University of Paris under Meillet, Lévi, Bloch, and Renou. He held professorships at Lyon, EPHE, and the Sorbonne.
Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval (1795–1871) was a linguist and scholar. He served as Professor of Vulgar Arabic at INALCO (1821–1871) and Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France (1833–1871).
Armin W. Geertz (born 1948) is a scholar in religious studies who held an academic post at Aarhus University, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2019.

Arnab Bhattacharya works in computational fields and Indology. Educated at IIT Bombay and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1997), he has served as a professor at TIFR and IIT Kanpur, and as Centre Director of the Homi Bhabha Centre.

Arnaldo Beltrami (born 1862) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Turin (~1881–1885). He taught at Liceo Ginnasio Luigi Galvani (1896–1931) and was a Docent of Greek at the University of Bologna.
Arnav Anjaria studied Tibetology and other fields, completing an integrated MA at the University of Hyderabad (2007–2014). He served as an Assistant Professor at Amity University from 2018 to 2019.

Arnold Adriaan Bake (1899–1963) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Leiden, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht under Willem Caland. He held research positions at Leiden and Brasenose College, and taught Sanskrit and Indian Music at SOAS.

Arnold C. Taylor (1867–1955) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Oxford (~1886–1890) and worked as a teacher at Uppingham School from circa 1890 to 1927.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a historian who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (PhD 1784). He spent his career at Göttingen as a lecturer and professor of philosophy and history.
Arnold Hirzel (1861–1931) was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Munich, and Leipzig, completing his Ph.D. at Leipzig in 1890 under Ernst Windisch.
